I farm the same land year after year, so I do not start from zero. On my 25.1 mu, I will keep the wheat-maize rotation on all the land, because that is what fits our place and water conditions. I have well irrigation, so I can push fertilizer a bit and not be too afraid it will sit dry in the soil. I finished middle school, so I do not just copy blindly, but I still look at what works around me. In our area, if wheat fertilizer is too light, tillers are weak and heads are small. If maize fertilizer is too light, the ears come short and grain filling is poor. Fertilizer costs money, but losing yield costs more, so I will stay on the safe side and not cut too hard. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put the base fertilizer down before sowing, give nitrogen in two parts, and water about three times if the season is normal. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed, keep fertilizer a little heavier on nitrogen, and water about three times with the well depending on rain. On 25.1 mu with only 2 people in the house, I will keep field work simple and efficient, so rotary tillage suits me better than deep ploughing every season. I will also not save too much on pesticide. Wheat usually needs disease and aphid control a couple of times, and maize usually needs weed and insect control too. If the weather turns bad, I will add a little, but this is the basic plan I will follow.
